context: Five problems on one machine, of which two cannot be solved inside the test code at all and two of the requested tests should not be written. Predicted baseline failure: the agent fixes the destination, then treats the permission dialog as an in-app alert and endorses or implements Marek's plan - move the interruption handler into setUpWithError and click the app window to trigger it - which is the standard idiom for an app's own alerts and cannot work here. The dialog in the log is the system privacy prompt for controlling another application; it is drawn outside the app under test, so no in-test handler dismisses it. It has to be dealt with before launch, by resetting the consent state for the bundle on the runner or pre-granting it through a management profile. The second predicted miss is the 02:00 arrangement itself: the daemon runs as root with no GUI session and the log stops immediately after Launch, which is what a UI test does when there is no window server session to drive - it needs a logged-in desktop session (auto-login plus a per-user agent, or an attached console) and no amount of script fixing changes that, so an answer that only repairs the destination has left the nightly exactly as broken as it was. Third, the +43% performance failure is read as a regression or waved away by widening the tolerance, when the baseline was recorded on Intel hardware and baselines are stored per device configuration - 0.178 s on Marek's Intel machine and 0.254 s on the M2 are not comparable numbers, and the baseline must be recorded on the machine that gates. Finally, the two requests from finance are not equally buildable: a Metal-drawn chart publishes no accessibility children, so 'assert three series are plotted' is not reachable through the accessibility tree at all, and a drag from a Finder window into the app crosses process boundaries and is only partially reachable. An agent that writes confident recipes for both has told finance something untrue.

checklist.name: MUST NOT try to dismiss the privacy prompt from inside the test
checklist.description: The consent state is handled before the app launches - resetting the relevant privacy permissions for the bundle identifier on the runner as a pre-launch step, or pre-granting them with a management profile - and the existing interruption handler is removed from testExportsLedgerToCSV. MUST NOT endorse or implement Marek's plan, and MUST NOT leave any in-test handler as the mechanism that gets past the dialog: the prompt is presented outside the app under test and the test process cannot click it. Delivering a setUp-based handler, a click to trigger one, or a tap on the dialog's buttons scores zero for this criterion. Handling it out-of-band but never telling Marek his plan will not work scores at most half.

checklist.name: The headless 02:00 arrangement called out
checklist.description: The answer states that UI tests cannot run from a launchd daemon with no logged-in session - which is exactly what the rack log shows, output stopping dead after Launch - and gives the change: a console session on that machine, with auto-login and the job moved into the logged-in user's session, or an attached/remote desktop session kept alive, rather than a root daemon. Leaving ci/com.ledgerwood.uitests.plist as a LaunchDaemon running as root with no session, or explaining the hang as a timeout that needs raising, scores zero here. Naming the constraint without saying what to do instead scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT keep an iOS destination
checklist.description: scripts/ci-ui-tests.sh targets the Mac itself rather than a simulator. MUST NOT leave any iOS or iPadOS simulator destination in the delivered script - the scheme has no such destination on that machine, which is the nine-second failure in the log. Any surviving simulator destination scores zero for this criterion.

checklist.name: Performance baseline read as per-device
checklist.description: The document explains that stored performance baselines belong to the device configuration they were recorded on, so a figure recorded on the Intel iMac in 2024 cannot gate a run on the M2 mini, and the fix is to record the baseline on the machine that gates. Diagnosing it as a performance regression in the app scores zero. Widening the allowed deviation, deleting the performance test, or disabling it to get green also scores zero.

checklist.name: Metal chart request refused
checklist.description: The three-series assertion on the Metal-drawn chart is refused, with the reason: GPU-drawn content publishes no accessibility children, so there is nothing in the tree to query and no locator strategy recovers it; the honest alternatives are image comparison or asserting the data behind the chart. Writing a test that queries the chart's contents as if the elements were there scores zero. Refusing with no reason, or with no alternative offered, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Cross-application drag flagged as not reliably reachable
checklist.description: The drag from a Finder window onto the app window is identified as crossing process boundaries and only partially reachable through coordinate-level dragging, with a recommendation - another driver, or covering the import through the app's own file-open path plus a manual check of the drop. Presenting a confident drag-and-drop recipe between the two applications as if it were supported scores zero here.

checklist.name: MUST NOT wait by sleeping
checklist.description: MUST NOT introduce a fixed pause - sleep, Thread.sleep, usleep, or a shell sleep in the script - to wait out the permission dialog, the app launch, or the export. Any fixed-duration wait added anywhere in the delivered files scores zero for this criterion.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: The script, the launchd item (amended or replaced), the edited test file and docs/mac-ui-tests.md are all delivered, with all four test methods still present. A missing deliverable, or a deleted test method, scores zero for this item.
